title: Jesus Expounds the Scriptures
summary: Jesus expounds the scriptures to the multitude and explains that the Father commanded him to give them these scriptures for future generations.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus expounded all things, great and small, to the multitude.
Jesus said the Father commanded him to give the people scriptures they had not previously had, for future generations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus teaches while the multitude listens.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, posture, and any scriptures physically present are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: These scriptures, which ye had not with you, the Father commanded that I should give unto you;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: he did expound all things unto them, both great and small.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict later events from Jesus's teaching as occurring visibly in the present.

title: The Scope of Jesus's Teaching
summary: Jesus teaches about events from the beginning through the last day, when all people stand before God to be judged, and about the two outcomes of resurrection.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus expounded events from the beginning until his coming in glory and described the earth and heavens passing away.
Jesus taught that all people, kindreds, nations, and tongues would stand before God to be judged according to their works.
Jesus taught of resurrection to everlasting life or damnation, according to mercy, justice, and holiness in Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus speaks to the multitude; the future events are reported as teaching and need not be shown as literal present events.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the future judgment, the people being judged, and the earth's passing away are not described as present visible events.

narration.text: all people, and all kindreds, and all nations and tongues shall stand before God, to be judged of their works,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The judgment and resurrection are teachings about future events, not a narrated present-time visual scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible judgment scene, divided groups, or descriptions of heaven or damnation.

title: The Record's Limits
summary: The narrator explains that the written account contains only a lesser part of Jesus's teachings, while Nephi's plates contain more, and that the record is intended to return to the people from the Gentiles.

explicit_facts.text: The book cannot contain even a hundredth part of what Jesus taught.
The plates of Nephi contain the greater part of what Jesus taught.
The narrator wrote a lesser part for it to be brought again to this people from the Gentiles, according to Jesus's words.

unspecified_visual_details: The narrator's identity and physical presence, the book, plates, and writing process are not specified in these verses.

narration.text: I have written them to the intent that they may be brought again unto this people,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is explanatory narration, not a described present-time writing scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unnamed writer or physical plates as present without textual support.

title: Faith and Greater Things
summary: The passage says the first things are given to try faith. If people believe, greater things will be made manifest to them; if they do not believe, those things will be withheld from them unto their condemnation.

explicit_facts.text: Receiving the first things is intended to try faith; belief is the condition for greater things to be made manifest.
If people do not believe, the greater things will be withheld from them unto their condemnation.

unspecified_visual_details: No people, physical setting, or visible manifestation are described.

narration.text: and if it shall so be that they shall believe these things then shall the greater things be made manifest unto them.
And if it so be that they will not believe these things, then shall the greater things be withheld from them, unto their condemnation.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are conditional teachings, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the greater things being manifested or withheld, or condemnation occurring, as specific visible events.
Do not invent a speaker, audience, or setting.

title: Mormon's Record
summary: Mormon reports that he was about to write what was engraved on Nephi's plates, but the Lord forbade it and said he would try his people's faith. Mormon says he writes what the Lord commanded, ends his sayings, and proceeds to write what was commanded.
characters: the Lord (reported speaker, not visibly present)

explicit_facts.text: Mormon reports that he was about to write what was engraved on Nephi's plates, but the Lord forbade it.
The Lord said he would try the faith of his people.
Mormon says he writes what the Lord commanded, ends his sayings, and proceeds to write what was commanded.

unspecified_visual_details: Mormon's appearance and location are not described.
The Lord's appearance is not described.
The verses do not specify whether an act of writing is visible, or describe writing implements.

spoken_dialogue.text: I will try the faith of my people.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the Lord (reported speech)

narration.text: Behold, I was about to write them, all which were engraven upon the plates of Nephi, but the Lord forbade it, saying:
Therefore I, Mormon, do write the things which have been commanded me of the Lord.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's words are reported by Mormon; no appearance is described.
Mormon's account of what he was about to write is past context, not a present-time action to stage.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly or invent an appearance for him.
Do not stage Mormon's earlier intention to write as a present-time event.
Do not invent Mormon's appearance, setting, writing implements, or additional dialogue.

title: The Lord Gives Bread to the People
summary: The Lord taught the people for three days. Afterward, he showed himself to them often and often broke, blessed, and gave them bread.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord taught the people for three days.
Afterward, he showed himself to them often.
He often broke bread, blessed it, and gave it to them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lord and some of the people could be shown during an occasion when he gives them bread.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the people's appearance, and the appearance of the bread are unspecified.

narration.text: and did break bread oft, and bless it, and give it unto them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The three days of teaching precede the later repeated appearances. The verse does not specify which occasion of giving bread is depicted.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the three days of teaching, repeated appearances, and bread-giving as one occasion.
Do not add a named location or spoken words.

title: Jesus Ministers to the Children
summary: Jesus teaches and ministers to the multitude's children, looses their tongues, and they speak great and marvelous things to their fathers.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus taught and ministered to the multitude's children and loosed their tongues.
The children spoke great and marvelous things to their fathers, greater than Jesus had revealed to the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The children speak while their fathers listen, with Jesus ministering to them.
unspecified_visual_details: The children's words, ages, appearances, and the specific manner of Jesus's ministry are unspecified.

narration.text: they did speak unto their fathers great and marvelous things,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The children's spoken content is not supplied and must not be invented.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the children's words or depict an unspecified supernatural spectacle.

title: Ascended into Heaven
summary: After healing their sick and lame, opening the eyes of their blind, unstopping the ears of the deaf, performing cures, and raising a man from the dead, he ascended into heaven and went unto the Father. The verse identifies this as following the second time he showed himself unto them.

explicit_facts.text: He healed their sick and lame, opened the eyes of their blind, unstopped the ears of the deaf, performed cures, and raised a man from the dead.
After the second time he showed himself unto them, he ascended into heaven and went unto the Father.

reasonable_visual_inferences: His ascent may be represented as an upward departure.
unspecified_visual_details: His appearance, the setting, and the visible manner of ascent are unspecified.

narration.text: and had ascended unto the Father

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The cures and raising of a man are recounted as completed events, not actions occurring during the ascent.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the reported cures or raising as simultaneous with the ascent.
Do not depict the Father; the verse does not describe an appearance.
Do not assign a name or location not supplied by this verse.

title: The Multitude Hears the Children
summary: The next day the multitude gathers and sees and hears the children, including babes, speak marvelous things that were forbidden to be written.

explicit_facts.text: On the morrow the multitude gathered and saw and heard the children.
Even babes opened their mouths and uttered marvelous things, which were forbidden to be written.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The gathered multitude watches and listens as children and babes speak.
unspecified_visual_details: The children's words, the number of people, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: the multitude gathered themselves together, and they both saw and heard these children;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The things the children uttered are explicitly not supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent or quote the children's utterances.

title: The Disciples Baptize and Teach
summary: The chosen disciples begin baptizing and teaching those who come to them; those baptized in Jesus's name are filled with the Holy Ghost, and many see and hear unspeakable things.
characters: people who came to the disciples

explicit_facts.text: The disciples Jesus chose began to baptize and teach those who came to them.
Those baptized in Jesus's name were filled with the Holy Ghost.
Many of them saw and heard things not lawful to be written.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A disciple baptizes a person while others gather to be taught.
unspecified_visual_details: The baptismal setting and manner, and the unspeakable things, are unspecified.

narration.text: began from that time forth to baptize and to teach as many as did come unto them;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 18 summarizes experiences without describing them; do not visualize their content.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Holy Ghost or unspeakable things in an invented form.

title: The People Minister to One Another
summary: The people teach and minister to one another, share all things in common, deal justly, and do as Jesus commanded; those baptized in Jesus's name are called the church of Christ.

explicit_facts.text: The people taught and ministered to one another and had all things common, dealing justly with one another.
They did all things as Jesus commanded them.
Those baptized in Jesus's name were called the church of Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People interact cooperatively and share with one another.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific shared goods, individual identities, and location are unspecified.

narration.text: they had all things common among them, every man dealing justly, one with another.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses describe a community practice, not a specific named gathering or transaction.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign names, biographies, or specific possessions to the people.
